exposure: non-use of routine intraoperative urinary catheterization during scheduled cesarean delivery
outcome: postoperative voiding patterns (time to and volume of first spontaneous void)
need for intervention for presumed urinary retention
cohort: 199 patients who underwent scheduled elective or repeat cesarean delivery without an intraoperative urinary catheter at an urban safety-net teaching institution, excluding those in labor, with twin gestations, or requiring a postpartum catheter.
finding: The mean time to the first postoperative void was 8.5 hours, and non-use of routine urinary catheters during scheduled cesarean delivery was associated with transient urinary retention in 19.6% of patients, but no increased sequelae at the time of discharge compared to those with an intraoperative catheter.
mod_finding: Non-use of routine urinary catheterization during scheduled cesarean delivery resulted in transient urinary retention in 19.6% of patients, but no increase in adverse sequelae by hospital discharge.
